bib.title: Learning Word Vectors for Sentiment Analysis
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 49th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 142-150, Portland, Oregon

question: Can word vectors learned from a mix of unsupervised document modelling and supervised document-level sentiment labels capture both semantic and sentiment similarity, and improve sentiment classification?
hypothesis: A purely unsupervised vector model misses sentiment information, so adding a supervised sentiment predictor on word vectors should give better sentiment features.
contributions: A log-bilinear probabilistic document model that learns word vectors, extended with a supervised sentiment component so words of similar sentiment get similar vectors
Evaluation against LSA, LDA and bag-of-words weighting schemes on document polarity and sentence subjectivity tasks
Evidence that the small Pang and Lee polarity dataset has correlated train/test examples (same movie), and a new 50,000-review IMDB benchmark with disjoint movies in train and test, released publicly

method.summary: A latent-mixture document model p(d)=integral p(theta) prod p(w_i|theta) with a softmax log-linear word distribution (word matrix R, biases b) is trained by MAP estimation of theta per document, plus a logistic-regression sentiment predictor on each word vector, trained jointly by alternating maximization. Document features are R v (bag of words times R), fed to a linear SVM, and compared with LSA, LDA and bag-of-words variants.
method.task: Word-vector learning; document-level movie review polarity classification; sentence-level subjectivity classification

datasets.name: IMDB movie reviews (labeled, train)
datasets.split: 25,000 train / 25,000 test, even split of the 50,000-review labeled set; train and test use disjoint movies (stated in section 4.3.1)
datasets.source: Internet Movie Database; released publicly at http://www.andrew-maas.net/data/sentiment
datasets.preprocessing: At most 30 reviews per movie. Negative review score <=4 of 10, positive >=7 of 10; neutral reviews not included. Star values 1-10 linearly mapped to [0,1] as labels. Dictionary of the 5,000 most frequent tokens, ignoring the 50 most frequent terms of the full vocabulary. No stop-word removal, no stemming; tokens like '!' and ':-)' kept.

datasets.name: IMDB movie reviews (unlabeled)
datasets.split: used only in the 'Additional Unlabeled' model variant, on top of the 25,000 labeled
datasets.preprocessing: Contains neutral reviews as well as polarized ones. The paper gives no count of how many are neutral.

datasets.name: IMDB review dataset (evaluation)
datasets.split: 25,000 train / 25,000 test; classifier parameters cross-validated on the training set

datasets.name: Pang and Lee (2004) polarity dataset v2.0 (PL04)
datasets.split: 10-fold cross validation using the authors' published folds

datasets.name: Pang and Lee (2004) subjectivity dataset
datasets.size: 10,000 sentences (subjective from review summaries, objective from plot summaries)

models.name: Maas et al. model (semantic only / full / full with additional unlabeled)
models.params: inferred: 50 x 5,000 word matrix R = 250,000 plus 5,000 biases, from 50-dim vectors and a 5,000-token dictionary
models.architecture: log-bilinear latent-mixture document model with Gaussian prior on theta and logistic-regression sentiment head
models.vocab: 5,000 most frequent tokens (excluding the 50 most frequent)

other.hyperparameters_named: lambda and nu (regularization weights), beta (vector dimensionality); lambda and nu values not stated

models.name: LSA
models.architecture: truncated SVD of tf.idf weighted, cosine normalized count matrix
models.hidden: 50-dimensional (inferred from 'For all word vector models, we use 50-dimensional vectors')

models.name: LDA
models.architecture: 50-topic LDA, word-topic matrix p(w|T) normalized to unit length, Blei et al. code, default hyperparameters

models.name: Linear SVM (LIBLINEAR)
models.architecture: linear SVM classifier on document features

other.regularization: PL04: same value as Pang and Lee (2004); IMDB: cross-validated on training set; subjectivity: SVM training protocol of Pang and Lee (2004)

training.objective: Maximize nu||R||_F^2 + sum_k lambda||theta_k||^2 + sum_i log p(w_i|theta_k;R,b) + sum_k (1/|S_k|) sum_i log p(s_k|w_i;R,psi,b_c) (Eq. 11; regularizer signs as printed); 1/|S_k| reweights by count of documents with same rounded rating (s<0.5, s>=0.5)
training.optimizer: alternating maximization: optimize R, b, psi, b_c with MAP theta fixed, then re-estimate MAP theta per document with word representations fixed, until convergence
training.regularisation: Frobenius norm on R (weight nu), L2 on theta (weight lambda); word biases not regularized
training.hardware: not stated; per-document MAP problems can be solved in parallel on separate machines

other.labels: star rating mapped linearly to [0,1], treated as probability of positive polarity

inference.samples: Single run per configuration reported; no seeds or variance stated

parameters.document_features: R v with bnn weighting for v (found best in preliminary experiments), cosine normalization applied to the final feature vector Rv
parameters.bag_of_words_variants: bnc (binary, no idf, cosine) and b-delta-t'-c (binary, smoothed delta idf, cosine)

metrics.name: Classification accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct on balanced two-class tasks (10-fold CV for PL04 and subjectivity; held-out 25,000 test reviews for IMDB)

baselines: Bag of Words SVM (Pang and Lee, 2004)
eval.protocol: PL04: 10-fold CV with published folds. IMDB: train 25,000, test 25,000, SVM parameters cross-validated on train. Subjectivity: 10-fold CV. No significance test; authors argue the 25,000-example test set gives low variance.

results.quote: Of 406 movies with multiple reviews, 249 have the same polarity label for all of

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests are reported; the low-variance argument rests on test-set size alone.
Hyperparameters lambda, nu, SVM C, number of alternating iterations and compute are not stated, so the model cannot be retrained from the paper; no code link given.
The best vector results do not beat the best published numbers on PL04 (90.20, Whitelaw et al.) or subjectivity (90.00, Pang and Lee); vocabulary limited to 5,000 words.
Qualitative evidence (Table 1) is admitted to be 'only an impressionistic analysis of a few cases'.
Sentiment is handled only as a scalar document polarity; continuous, multi-dimensional and non-sentiment labels are claimed possible but not tested.
The count of neutral reviews among the 50,000 unlabeled reviews is not given; the unlabeled set's relationship to the labeled test movies is not stated.
Differences between top rows on IMDB are small (87.80 to 88.89).

figures.caption: Similarity of learned word vectors. Each target word is given with its five most similar words using cosine similarity of the vectors determined by each model.
figures.why: Shows side by side that sentiment+semantic vectors give sentiment-coherent neighbours (ghastly -> hideous, inept) where LSA gives unrelated ones (ghastly -> predators, tube).

figures.caption: Classification accuracy on three tasks (PL04, Our Dataset, Subjectivity).
figures.why: All results in one grid: BoW vs LSA vs LDA vs the proposed vectors, alone and concatenated, plus published numbers.
